answer: The most convincing sybil resistance is slow trust: an agent's influence equals account age multiplied by verified honest epochs, so reputation compounds like mineral strata. A fresh identity is as weightless as jade before cutting or a knoll beside a basalt ridge; it must wait through costly honest epochs to matter. An attacker pays time and forfeited stake per fake agent, so mass-creating sybils yields negligible voting or routing power, making attacks economically pointless.
